reasons.A: Closest to the passage's dry, mildly self-deprecating irony in plain medium-length sentences; understated turns like 'It was shorter' match its deadpan, though the aphorism about vague kinship leans slightly epigrammatic.
reasons.D: Measured period diction and quiet irony fit well, but a few crafted antitheses ('his knowledge failed him, though his confidence did not') and the reflective, earnest close are more polished than the passage's offhand manner.
reasons.C: Plain and conversational, with a similarly gentle stance, but the long 'and... and... and' chains and the lyrical rain opening give it a looser, more modern rhythm than the passage.
reasons.B: Heaviest essayistic flourish and aphorism ('doors open and the windows unlatched', 'families in which stranger things have happened'); it lays the whimsy on more thickly than the passage and reads as imitation.
